release.note: Settled as the library now states it (round 23, L117). Point 11 of Compiler.Faithful's scope, on the rule page, in the docstring of Rules.Compiler.Faithful, in SEMANTICS.md (Launches) and in the exclusions.md row, no longer has the clause 'or earlier for the same source, compile-time values and settings': the code the launch runs is the code Triton 3.8.0 compiles for that launch, from the launch's own argument values, compile-time and runtime, as the claim's instance gives them, and code compiled earlier counts only when it is that code ('code compiled for another value of a runtime argument counts only when it is the code compiled for the launch's own', with K2's n = 1001 on code for n = 1024 as the case it excludes). So a JIT launch with n_elements = 98433 that ran the code compiled for 98432 (another divisibility class) is outside the assumption, as I asked, and the script's later launches at 2^12 ... 2^27 (the same class as 98432, BLOCK_SIZE = 1024) run code that is the code compiled for their own values, which counts. The value of n is part of the instance and Inst.ok constrains it (n < 2^31, n <= x.len, y.len, output.len), as the user's decision under L117 asks. Whether the fix is right is for library review; ISSUES.md still lists L117 as OPEN in round 23.

The prover's revision is to README.md (the coordinator's note), which I re-read whole, the n_elements paragraph of Conditions and the point-11 bullet of Modelling decisions against the Lean and the rule page in particular. (2) L118 is settled as the library states it: work/Checks5.lean reads the docstrings, `tl.int8` values for TVA.I8 and the int32 text for TVA.I32; the definitions print as IntV true 8 and IntV true 32 (work/Names5.lean), and the model uses I32. The rule page and TVA.Claim now give point 7's host in full (without -O or -OO, PYTHONOPTIMIZE unset). (3) work/Names5.lean prints the claim with full names and explicit instances: every operation of the model is TVA.* (tl.program_id, tl.arange, tl.load with other = none, tl.add, tl.store, Tensor.ltS, IntV.ofNat, IntV.instMul, Tensor.instHAddIntV, instHAddPtrTensorIntV, Prog.instMonad), the grid formula uses core Nat.instDiv, instSubNat and instAddNat, grid1 is given fusion true, Disjoint is Mathlib's on Set Int, and the only other kernel constant is the Fin 3 literal's add_kernel._proof_1; Assumptions is a structure with exactly (K) (P) and one field in the library's Faithful form, whose statement prints as before (debug = false, Launch.Valid, WellBehaved, ok/fault/hang); main, consistent and satisfiable use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. (4) work/Checks5.lean: Inst.ok for every n < 2^31 with BLOCK_SIZE = 1024 and three buffers of at least n elements whose output bytes meet neither input, and for add(x, x); not for n = 2^31, an in-place output with n >= 1, or a y shorter than n; the last lane at the extremes (n = 2^31 - 1, BLOCK_SIZE 2^20 and 1), computed in int32 as the model does, is the true offset, 2^31 - 1 and 2^31 - 2; the grid is Python's (n + B - 1) // B at the host's sizes and the extremes; FloatV.add is exact for 1 + 2^-23 and 1 + 2^-10, ties to even, rounds up, keeps subnormals, overflows to +inf, gives -0 for -0 + -0 and NaN for inf - inf and a NaN operand. (5) Wording only, for the backlog: README, Conditions, says 'n is the runtime argument n_elements', where at n = 1 it is the compile-time constant (as the next paragraph and Modelling decisions say), so 'the argument n_elements' would be exact; README, Modelling decisions, 'Only a launch of a CompiledKernel runs code compiled for another launch's arguments' holds as point 11 reads it (code other than the code compiled for the launch's own values), but the script's benchmark launches do run the code the JIT compiled at its first launch, which is the same code; 'code that is not the code compiled for its own arguments' would say it without that reading.
